newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Westpac Australia consumer index down in Sept.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Westpac Australia consumer index down in Sept.

text.p: The Westpac/Melbourne Institute consumer sentiment index for September fell 1.3 points or 1.2 percent to 105.5, following a 0.3 point fall in August.

Westpac chief economist Bill Evans said this latest fall wiped out all the boost that followed the Coalition election victory in March. However, this was the first survey since the tough Federal 1996/97 budget in August and in that respect compared favourably with past reactions to budgets, he said.
"Although the budget is expected to deliver the largest contraction of government spending in recent decades, the impact on sentiment has been quite subdued," Evans said.
Evans noted that following first term budgets in 1987, 1990 and 1993 the sentiment index had fallen 3.6 percent, 6.7 percent and 9.4 percent respectively.

"While the sentiment index has fallen 5.5 percent from its post-election high, it remains at comparatively high levels," Evans said. "Only in 1984 and 1994 has the average index for the year exceeded current levels."
The major shift in September was that consumers were less convinced it was a good time to buy major household items.
"That outcome suggests recent subdued levels of consumer spending will continue in the near term," Evans said.
The overall sentiment index was well down on the 111.7 high seen in March but still up 2.6 percent on September 1995.

The proportion of consumers thinking it was a good time to buy a major household items fell to 49 percent from 54 percent in August while those thinking it a bad time rose to 23 percent from 20 percent.
The net balance of those thinking the economy would improve over the coming year improved to minus 4.0 from minus 6.0, and over the next five years to minus 6.0 from minus 9.0.
